subject.title: [Feature]: Include interaction metadata in Discord button callbacks

question: Should generic Discord component callbacks expose a new agent-visible structured interaction metadata envelope, and which fields are public versus plugin-only?
rationale: The request is useful and source-reproducible, but it adds a public inbound context contract and exposes identifiers/callback data across a security-sensitive trust boundary.

options.title: Add a bounded typed envelope
options.body: Expose documented fields such as interaction kind, originating message id, component id or safe callback data, label/selected values, and clicker identity with tests that preserve plugin opaque-data semantics.

options.title: Keep metadata plugin-only
options.body: Document that generic callbacks remain normal text inbound messages and require stateful workflows to use plugin interactive handlers or explicit app state.

options.title: Ship a narrower first contract
options.body: Expose only source message and sender identifiers now, then defer custom/callback data semantics until the command and trust-boundary policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Add a bounded typed envelope
recommendation.body: Expose documented fields such as interaction kind, originating message id, component id or safe callback data, label/selected values, and clicker identity with tests that preserve plugin opaque-data semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent inbound metadata and plugin/channel boundary work makes this the clearest owner for the public contract decision.
